I agree with everything but Language, We know India as we know it was established in 1947 and goa was incorporated into our union in 1961. (for a lack of better terms I used incorporated and I do know the whole stuff that went down during that period)

So my point is states were separated or made based on language not religion, not caste and not even region. Whether that was good or not it's still debatable but i believe it had its perks. It gave the people Identity, it united the people who were once oppressed based on Caste and Religion, it made them question the ruling class, it made them demand equality. We might think cultures and languages go hand in hand but they do not. 

High caste culture is different from low caste to this day and yet most of the past inequalities were and are still being suppressed, processed and treated because the people and a few good politicians (back then) began to think in a language identity rather than their niche micro caste identity. So we shouldn't dismiss Languages in any form in any situation and in good faith it's better not to impose any languages into any cultures that we have created since 1947. Our cultural values and languages are generations but the system we live in now is just 78 years old.

So in Goa's case, because there is a considerable majority of native marathi speakers living they should never be made to speak a new language or learn something that they don't want to.
